did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 36 begins with Elihu continuing his speech, following his words in the previous chapters.
Did you know? Elihu presents God as “mighty”—great in power—yet also as one who does not despise anyone or act arbitrarily.
Did you know? According to Elihu, God does not preserve the wicked without judgment; at the same time, he ensures justice and protection for the poor.
Did you know? Elihu describes people trapped in “fetters” and the cords of affliction—a picture of distress and bondage, whether literal or symbolic.
Did you know? According to Elihu’s speech, suffering can reveal a person’s ways and turn them toward instruction and repentance.
Did you know? Elihu distinguishes between those who listen and serve God, ending their days in prosperity, and those who do not listen.
Did you know? Elihu says that God rescues the poor from their affliction and uses their suffering to make them listen.
Did you know? Addressing Job, Elihu describes the possibility that God will lead him from distress into a broad place, rest, and a table filled with abundance.
Did you know? Elihu emphasizes that God is exalted in power, and no one can teach him his way or command him.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, Elihu describes water descending from the heavens: drops evaporate and become rain in the clouds, which falls on many people.
